content: 1. Strong inducers of the enzyme CYP3A4 significantly reduce the systemic exposure of ivacaftor, approximately by ninefold. Close monitoring is required. 2. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. 3. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ivosidenib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Coadministration of ivosidenib with strong CYP3A4 inducers decreases plasma concentrations of ivosidenib. Alternative therapies should be considered. 5. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ixazomib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong inducers decrease ixazomib's Cmax by 54% and AUC by 74%. Close monitoring is required. 7. Rifampin decreases ketamine levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Rifampin reduces ketoconazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Ketoconazole also decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 9. Rifampin decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic metabolism and clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Rifampin reduces lansoprazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of the CYP2C19 interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 11. Rifampin decreases lapatinib levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Rifampin reduces larotrectinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, double the larotrectinib dose and resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inducer for 3–5 half-lives. 13. Lasmiditan increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Rifampin decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction reduces sofosbuvir's conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007), responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. Coadministration is contraindicated. 15. Rifampin reduces lefamulin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 16. Rifampin increases leflunomide effects by enhancing its metabolism to its active metabolite. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Rifampin decreases lemborexant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor CYP2B6 substrates for adequate clinical response. 18. Rifampin reduces lenacapavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. 19. Rifampin decreases leniolisib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Rifampin reduces lesinurad levels or effects by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Rifampin decreases letermovir levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Rifampin reduces levamlodipine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 23. Rifampin decreases levoketoconazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Levoketoconazole also reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Rifampin reduces levonorgestrel levels (both intrauterine and oral) by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; alternative or backup contraception is recommended during enzyme inducer use and for 28 days after discontinuation. 25. Rifampin decreases levothyroxine levels by increasing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Rifampin reduces lidocaine levels or effects by altering CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Rifampin decreases linagliptin levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended. 28. Rifampin reduces liothyronine levels by increasing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Rifampin decreases lisinopril levels by increasing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Rifampin reduces lofepramine levels by increasing metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 31. Lomitapide increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Rifampin decreases lomitapide levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Rifampin reduces lonafarnib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. 33. Rifampin decreases loperamide levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Rifampin reduces lopinavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Rifampin decreases loratadine levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Rifampin reduces lorlatinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. Discontinue the inducer for three plasma half-lives before initiating lorlatinib. 37. Rifampin decreases losartan levels or effects by altering CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Rifampin reduces lovastatin levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Rifampin decreases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A inducers minimally affect lumacaftor exposure but reduce ivacaftor exposure (AUC) by 57%, potentially reducing efficacy. 40. Rifampin reduces lumateperone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Rifampin decreases lumefantrine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated due to reduced serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. 42. Rifampin reduces lurasidone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. 43. Rifampin decreases lurbinectedin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Rifampin reduces macimorelin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration may lead to false-positive test results; discontinue the inducer with sufficient washout time before testing. 45. Rifampin decreases macitentan levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Rifampin reduces maraviroc levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Rifampin decreases marijuana levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Rifampin reduces mavacamten levels or effects by altering CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 49. Rifampin increases mavorixafor levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Rifampin decreases mavorixafor levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Rifampin reduces medroxyprogesterone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible; close monitoring is required. 51. Rifampin decreases mefloquine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 52. Rifampin reduces melatonin levels or effects by altering CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Rifampin decreases meloxicam levels by increasing metabolism through CYP2C9/10. The clinical significance is unknown. 54. Rifampin reduces mestranol levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Contraceptive failure is possible. 55. Rifampin decreases methadone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Rifampin reduces methylprednisolone levels or effects by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 57. Rifampin decreases metoprolol levels by increasing metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Rifampin reduces mexiletine levels or effects by altering CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Rifampin decreases miconazole vaginal levels by increasing metabolism. Miconazole vaginal also reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 60. Rifampin reduces midazolam levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Rifampin decreases midostaurin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
